hypothesis: The persistent 2014 abnormal ROA is mainly FX.
interpretation: January FX explains overshoot timing, but annual abnormality is securities-led.

hypothesis: The +1.4pp securities gap is the net abnormal bank benefit.
evidence: ROA gap is only +0.7pp because admin, taxes, income tax and other offsets absorb part of the gross gain.
interpretation: Gross component gap can exceed net ROA gap.

hypothesis: H1-2018 +0.4pp abnormal ROA is an FX-only effect.
evidence: BCRA names titles, CER, interest income and FX as positive margin drivers; services and credit losses offset; admin costs improve.
interpretation: May is FX-heavy, H1 bridge is multicomponent.

hypothesis: Q4-23 +9pp ROA gap equals the FX gap.
evidence: FX +11.3pp exceeds net ROA gap; passes +7.7 and securities +7.3 also positive, while monetary result -9.2 and taxes/funding/costs offset.
interpretation: Large positive gross channels coexist with large negatives.

hypothesis: Q4 component gaps identify effects after 10 Dec.
evidence: Q4 contains Oct-Nov pre-shock; V49 documented strong pretrend.
interpretation: Label as Q4 abnormal components, not post-Dec components.

hypothesis: Lower credit costs explain abnormal positive ROA.
evidence: 2018 credit-loss contribution is -0.3pp; Q4-23 is -1.2pp; 2014 annual only +0.1pp.
interpretation: Credit costs mostly offset rather than create abnormal positive results.

hypothesis: A positive FX/titles/CER gap is a transfer from households.
evidence: These are bank balance/result categories without one-to-one household counterparty identity.
interpretation: Component bridge identifies accounting source, not distributive transfer.
